**A drive that has lost its top folder list no longer looks like a wrong
password** when its folder also holds files from other drives. Cloak now
says what's going on and lets you open it as your drive.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.6.1-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.6.1-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again). macFUSE's kernel extension must be
allowed; on Apple Silicon that means its one-time Reduced Security setup.

## Fixed

- **A drive missing its top folder list, with other drives' files in its
  folder,** said "wrong password" even with the right one. **Unlock** and
  **Add existing drive** now explain the situation and how many of the
  folder's hidden items the password opens, and offer **Open as this
  drive**. That rebuilds the drive's top list, so from then on it unlocks
  as usual, and the other drives' files wait to be brought in.

  Cloak asks rather than deciding because, without the keys, that folder
  looks the same as another drive's folder holding some of this drive's
  files. Choosing it by mistake loses nothing: both drives then share the
  folder, each opens with its own password, and each sees the other's files
  as waiting to be brought in.

## Known limitations

- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
- Hidden files of the same drive can be shown to belong together (they share
  the lock's salt); a file on its own looks random.
